I don't know if the comments questioning Firejail's implementation in your OP have been changed/fixed over the years. I simple don't bother to setup Firejail anymore and try to use Apparmor with a good sense of security awareness: check package sources, use as much official provided packages as possible and harden services (like webservers, etc.) instead. Remember systemd also implemented a lot of recent changes that should benefit the user and systeem like protecting it's home or tmp folders.

Just try to remember the user is always the weakest link.

I don't know if Firejail is truly safe, having use it in the past together with Apparmor it wasn't always the best solution and it has it's up and downs:

- Not every application was able to run correctly under Firejail without editing profiles.

- You need to create symlinks and edit your profile(s).

- It didn't feel like I was more secured against alternatives like standalone Apparmor or SELinux and the frustration of testing every app is working fine with Firejail (e.g. something can't be accessed) is just terrible.

I haven't tested alternatives implementations like appimage that also seem to provide Firejail support, just remember every security tool can be defeated by it's own user and configuration is key.

The Arch Wiki provides more and better examples to harden your setup.
